Explain the example for sort and limit graph results

blocks.text: ORDER BY sorts returned rows from a graph query. LIMIT keeps only the chosen number.
Use Neo4j 5+ locally with Neo4j Browser or another Cypher editor. These queries use fictional cma-prefixed ids. Cypher is not SQL and does not run in this site's SQL playground.

blocks.code: MATCH (b:Book) WHERE b.id STARTS WITH 'cma-' RETURN b.title,b.pages ORDER BY b.pages,b.title LIMIT 1;
blocks.title: Sort and limit graph results

blocks.text: Read the code step by step

items: `ORDER BY` chooses a result order. Include a tie-break field when equal values need a stable order.
`WHERE` keeps only rows that pass its condition. Check the condition with sample data before using it for a change.
`MATCH` finds the described graph pattern. Labels and arrow direction narrow the connections being followed.

blocks.text: With the two sample books, Garden Days is the shortest result.

blocks.title: A mistake to avoid
blocks.text: The graph model does not give results a useful default order. State the order when it matters.

blocks.title: Your small task
blocks.text: Return the longest sample book instead.
